notes: Gemma 4 E4B (thinking off) gets one conversation per clip in its chat template: the system prompt, then one user turn with the user prompt first and the audio after it (as the model card advises), with the system and user prompts of `scripts/llm_eval/prompts.yaml` (the same as for GPT Realtime); the clip as 16 kHz mono (at most its first 30 s)

Greedy decoding (do_sample=False, no repetition penalty), at most 24 new tokens, bfloat16 on `mps`, sdpa attention; so the answers are the same from run to run (up to rounding differences between devices)

The answer is read by `scripts/llm_eval/parsing.py` and becomes a one-hot vector over the 7 emotions plus `invalid`. An answer that is not exactly one label gets a follow-up in the same conversation ("Answer with exactly one word from this list, in lowercase, and nothing else: angry, disgusted, fearful, happy, neutral, sad, surprised."), up to 1 time(s); then `invalid`
An answer that is not one of the dataset's emotions counts as wrong (column *other answer* of the confusion matrices); the raw answers are in `outputs/gemma4_e4b/responses.jsonl`

columns.audio_path: audio file, relative to the emotion_recognition/ folder
columns.acted_emotion: ground truth: the emotion each actor was asked to portray, from the third number in the file name (01 neutral, 02 calm, 03 happy, 04 sad, 05 angry, 06 fearful, 07 disgust, 08 surprised)
columns.prediction: model prediction: the most probable of the 7 emotions evaluated (neutral, happy, sad, angry, fearful, disgusted, surprised)
columns.prediction_all_classes: model prediction: the most probable of all 8 model classes
columns.p_*: model probability of each of its 8 classes (they add up to 1)
columns.token_p_*: audio LLMs: the model's probability of each label at the first generated position (first-token probabilities, renormalised over the labels; they add up to 1); the prediction is still the parsed answer
columns.token_mass: audio LLMs: the share of the whole vocabulary that the labels' first tokens get at that position
